# Elements

Elements is a component framework for building application UI with LLMs and humans working together.

Primary docs:
- Overview: /elements
- AI builder guide: /elements/ai
- Theming: /elements/theming
- Studio: /elements/components/studio
- Blocks: /elements/blocks/dashboard
- Components: /elements/components/button
- Headless web components: /elements/headless

Philosophy:
- Prefer composition over invention.
- Use Elements primitives for behaviour and accessibility.
- Use visual primitives for surfaces and layout polish.
- Use blocks for complete app screens and common product patterns.
- Keep generated UI editable in Studio.
- Use token-based theming names such as bg-background, text-foreground, bg-card, text-card-foreground, bg-popover, text-popover-foreground, bg-primary, text-primary-foreground, bg-secondary, text-secondary-foreground, text-muted-foreground, border-border, border-input, ring-ring, bg-success, bg-warning, and bg-destructive.
- Do not use raw colours unless defining a theme.
- Prefer component props for behaviour and classes for layout, spacing, and small visual adjustments.
- Give generated nodes stable ids and human labels when returning Studio specs.

Current component families:
- Behaviour components: Button, Dropdown, Dialog, Drawer, Tabs, Toggle, Tooltip, Accordion, Menu, Listbox, Combobox, Autocomplete, Popover, Toast, Command palette.
- Form components: Checkbox, Radio group, Text input, Password input, Textarea, Code input, JSON input, JSON list input, Number input, Select input, Native select, Boolean input, Color input.
- Visual components: Card.
- Blocks: Dashboard, Chat, Mail, Forms, Login.

LLM generation rules:
1. Choose an existing block when the request matches a known app pattern.
2. Choose existing components before writing custom HTML.
3. Keep accessibility inside components; do not recreate keyboard navigation by hand.
4. Prefer native form behaviour where it is useful, especially on mobile.
5. Use Code input for prompts, templates, snippets, and structured text that benefits from a code editor.
6. Use JSON input for editable schemas, tool payloads, app config, and other parsed structured data.
7. Use JSON list input for schema-aware arrays of objects, especially inspector editors for menu items, commands, options, toasts, and people lists.
8. Return an editable Studio spec when the user may want to inspect or revise the UI later.
9. Use clear layer labels and stable ids in specs.
10. Do not invent new theme colour names; use the theme page token names.
11. Keep generated interfaces dense, practical, and product-like unless the user asks for a marketing page.

Future AI-specific areas:
- AI chat tools that return editable UI.
- Voice tools and multimodal controls.
- Agent task runners that stream status into UI.
- Server-backed autocomplete and search patterns.
- Tool-call result renderers.
